Brick-by-Brick Masonry
Good walls are made one course at a time.

Brick-by-Brick masonry lets you build brick and stone blocks in place, using a masonry trowel, mortar, and matching fired bricks. Instead of placing a finished block all at once, you begin with a partial construction course and work it upward with the trowel until it becomes a finished block, slab, or stair.

Getting Started
First make a trowel. Metal trowels are made by smithing a trowel head, then fitting it to a stick in the crafting grid. The trowel must also be filled with mortar; rightmouse-click a bucket or other suitable liquid container with the trowel to refill it.

To place brick construction courses, keep the trowel in your main hand and hold the matching fired brick in your offhand. Brick-setting steps require the correct brick color, so a red course needs red fired bricks, a tan course needs tan fired bricks, and so on.

Trowel Modes
Use the tool mode key to switch the trowel between building, slab placement, stair placement, and block placement. Slab, stair, and block modes start new construction courses. Build mode continues an existing course, alternating between spreading mortar and setting the next fired brick.

Each successful step consumes mortar from the trowel. Brick-setting steps also consume one matching fired brick from the offhand. If the trowel is empty, or a brick-setting step has the wrong brick held, the course will not advance.

Construction Courses
Brick block courses are built in several stages and finish as a completed brick block. Slab and stair courses begin as partial shapes, then resolve into the matching finished slab or stair once the last stage is completed. These construction stages can be found in the Brick-by-Brick creative tab, but in normal play they are meant to be placed and advanced with the trowel.

Cobblestone courses work in the same spirit, using stone construction stages instead of fired brick courses. They are intended for rough stone construction where the block is assembled in place rather than placed fully formed.

Making Mortar
Liquid mortar is mixed in a barrel from mortar and water. Liquid clay is mixed from clay and water, and may be used by later Brick-by-Brick systems. Refractory mortar is available as its own liquid material for high-temperature masonry work.
